hints: Notice you are given $12 \text{ V}$ and $1.4 \text{ A}$ for the 3.0 m wire, so first find its resistance $R$ from $V$ and $I$.
Connect $R$ to dimensions with $R = \rho L/A$, where $\rho = 4.9 \times 10^{-7} \text{ } \Omega \text{ m}$ and $L = 3.0 \text{ m}$.
Rearrange to $A = \rho L/R$, substitute $R \approx 8.57 \text{ } \Omega$, and check the power of ten gives $10^{-7} \text{ m}^2$.
walkthrough: Find the wire resistance from the measured p.d. and current: $R = V/I = 12/1.4$.
Calculate $R \approx 8.57 \text{ } \Omega$ and keep the unit $\Omega$ for the next substitution.
Use the resistivity relation $R = \rho L/A$ and rearrange for area: $A = \rho L/R$.
Calculate $A \approx 1.47 \times 10^{-6}/8.57 \approx 1.7 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}^2$, which has the correct unit for area. This is option B.

options.A: Too small by about 30%. It does not follow from $A = \rho L / R$ with $R = 12/1.4$.
options.B: Follows from $R = V/I$ and $A = \rho L/R$, giving about $1.7 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}^2$.
options.C: About 10 times too large. It suggests a power-of-ten slip when combining $4.9 \times 10^{-7}$ with $R \approx 8.6 \text{ } \Omega$.
options.D: Much too large because it uses $I/V$ for resistance instead of $V/I$, giving $R \approx 0.12 \text{ } \Omega$.
